title: אֶכְרַע אֶקֹּד | Ekhra’ Eqqod, a rəshut for Nishmat on Rosh haShanah by Rabbi Yoav ben Yeḥiel of Rome
author: Isaac Gantwerk Mayer (transcription & naqdanut)

coauthors.name: Isaac Gantwerk Mayer (transcription & naqdanut)
coauthors.bio: From a family of musicians, Isaac Gantwerk Mayer believes that creative art is one of the most powerful ways to get in touch with the divine. He composes music and poetry in Hebrew and English. (He also translates and authors his own original works.) coauthors.name: Yoav ben Yeḥiel of Rome
coauthors.bio: Yoav ben Yeḥiel (fl. 14th c.) was a paytan of fourteenth century Rome. He belonged to the Beth-El family, and was the author of five piyyuṭim (inserted in the Roman Maḥzor) for Passover, having for their subject the Canticles, and piyyuṭim for Shavu'ot and Rosh ha-Shanah (before "Nishmat"), and for Yom Kippur (before "Ḳaddish"). In the Roman Maḥzor, also, a prayer entitled "Ashmurot ha-Boḳer" for Thursdays on which the "Taḥanun" is not recited, is signed "Joab"; and a seliḥah bearing the same signature is found in the seliḥot collection at Tripoli. Yoav is believed to be identical with the young poet whom Immanuel satirized ("Maḥberot," viii. 66).

content:
This rəshut, or introductory piyyuṭ, is recited in the Italian rite before Nishmat Kol Ḥai on (the first day) of Rosh haShanah. It was written by the fourteenth-century payṭan R. Yoav ben Yeḥiel of Rome. Also included is a rhyming acrostic translation.
Source (Hebrew) Translation (English)
אֶכְרַע אֶקֹּד לִפְנֵי מַלְכִּי
אֶקְרָאֶה מִפָּנָיו אַבְרֵךְ
שׁוֹפֵט יָשָׁר הוּא אֵלִי, כִּי
יוֹרֶ֖ה חַטָּאִ֣ים בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃
אֶכְרַע אֶקֹּד…
Before my Sovereign I bend and bow;
let me call “Great One!” before Their face!
An upright judge is my God, and how
They teach the sinners to find their place![1] Psalms 25:8 
Before my Sovereign…
יוֹם זֶה יוֹם הַדִּין הוּא נִקְרָא
מִשְׁפָּט הוּא לֵאלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב
יֹשֵׁב עַל־כִּסֵּא רָם נוֹרָא
וּלְמִישׁוֹר יַיְשִׁיר הֶעָקֹב
עַל־הֶאָח תּוֹךְ אֵשׁ בּוֹעֲרָה
יַבְעִיר כׇל־אָח֙ עָק֣וֹב יַעְקֹ֔ב
לָכֵן אַתְּ שׁוֹכֶֽבֶת חֵיקִי
הִתְנַחֲמִי סִפְקִי עַל־יָרֵךְ
עַל־בָּמוֹת יֵֽצֶר לֵב דִּרְכִי
תִּרְדִּי בוֹ בַּעֲבוֹדַת פָּֽרֶךְ׃
אֶכְרַע אֶקֹּד…
Judgement Day this day is called
as is the rule from Jacob’s God!
On an awesome throne They sit over all,
to set to straight the bent and flawed!
And in the brazier the fire will scald
to burn each brother engaged in fraud![2] Jeremiah 9:3 
So you[3] The soul  who sleep in me for now,
regret and strike your thigh, abased,
upon the urge’s shrines, stomp, plough,
with toil it will be displaced!
Before my Sovereign…
וּבִתְרוּעַת מֶֽלֶךְ עוּרִי
וּבִתְקֹֽעַ שׁוֹפָר שִׁמְעִי
וּבִשְׁבָרִים יִצְרֵךְ שִׁבְרִי
הַשְׁפִּֽילִי אוֹתוֹ הַכְנִֽיעִי
וּזְדוֹן עׇרְלַת לֵב הָסִֽירִי
הוֹחִילִי לֵאלֹהֵי יִשְׁעִי.
שֽׁוּבִי שׁוּלַמִּית עָדָיו, כִּי
חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם הוּא אַף אֶֽרֶךְ
גּוֹאֵ֣ל מִשַּׁ֣חַת חַיָּ֑יְכִי
אֵין לוֹ דִּמְיוֹן אַף לֹא עֵֽרֶךְ׃
אֶכְרַע אֶקֹּד…
On Sovereign blasting do arise,
at shofar’s trumpets hear the sound!
And break your urge in broken cries,
subdue it that it may be downed!
The pompous foreskinned heart abscise;
trust God in whom salvation is found.
Return, o Shulamite, to Them somehow,
for They are patient and full of grace,
They free your soul from shadowed clough,[4] Psalms 103:4 
though lacking form in concrete space!
Before my Sovereign…
אֵל דָּרַשׁ סֵֽפֶר, וַיִּקְרָא
אַיֵּה שֹׁקֵל אַיֵּה סֹפֵר
וּלְצַדִּיק דּוֹרֵךְ הַיְשָׁרָה
דּוֹדִי לִי אֶשְׁכּוֹל הַכֹּֽפֶר
וּרְשָׁעִים יִשְׁתּוּ מֵי מָרָה
אוֹכֶֽלֶת אֵשׁ כׇּל־הַכּוֹפֵר.
וּמִמַּחֲצִית פִּשְׁעִי עֶרְכִּי
מַעֲבִיר רִאשׁוֹן צוּר מִתְבָּרֵךְ
וּמַכְרִֽיעַ מֹאזְנֵי צִדְקִי
וּמֵשִׂים פְּעָמַי לַדֶּֽרֶךְ׃
אֶכְרַע אֶקֹּד…
Asking to the book, God said:
“Where is the surveyor, where the scribe?”
To the righteous who straightly tread,
My Love, like henna to describe.
While fire on heretics is fed,
the cruel a bitter brew imbibe.
If You from half my crimes endow,
the blessed Rock skips the first case.
My righteous scale They do allow,
and set upon the path my pace.
Before my Sovereign…
בִּינוּ־נָא זֹאת הָאֵל דִּרְשׁוּ
מִיּוֹם דִּין עַד־יוֹם כַּפָּרָה
וּבִנְתַּֽיִם פָּנָיו בַּקְּשׁוּ
לֹא יַשְׁחִית בַּעֲבוּר הָעֲשָׂרָה
וּבְכׇל־לֵב אוֹתוֹ תַקְדִּֽישׁוּ
הוּא יַצִּילְכֶם מִכׇּל־צָרָה.
גַּם אַתְּ נַפְשִׁי אֵלִי בָּרְכִי
וּלְפָנָיו הַכְרִֽיעִי בֶֽרֶךְ
הוּא יִגְמֹל חֶֽסֶד עָלָֽיְכִי
ק֥וּמִי א֖וֹרִי כִּ֣י בָ֣א אוֹרֵ֑ךְ
אֶכְרַע אֶקֹּד…
Bear this in mind: for God inquire
from Judgement Day to that of Amends.
Between them, let Their face inspire,
That on the Tenth nothing incends.
Wholeheartedly be Their sanctifier,
For They will save you from bad ends.
You too, my soul, to God avow,
Before Them bend the knee and brace;
They repay your goodness; now,
Arise and shine, your light makes haste![5] Isaiah 60:1 
Before my Sovereign…

 

Notes

Notes
1 Psalms 25:8
2 Jeremiah 9:3
3 The soul
4 Psalms 103:4
5 Isaiah 60:1
